paragraphs.text: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III (FHH3) is an autosomal dominant disorder of extracellular calcium homeostasis. Like FHH1 and FHH2, it is characterized by lifelong elevation of serum calcium with inappropriately low urinary calcium excretion. Nesbit et al. (2013) noted that, unlike FHH1 and FHH2, FHH3 is characterized by increased serum PTH concentrations, hypophosphatemia, and osteomalacia. Howles et al. (2016) described FHH3 as the most clinically severe of the 3 types of familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia.

paragraphs.text: McMurtry et al. (1992) studied a large kindred with familial benign (hypocalciuric) hypercalcemia. After the proposita was identified, 46 kindred members spanning 5 generations and aged 1.5 to 91 years were surveyed biochemically and/or by chart review, and 19 were affected. In the 15 hypercalcemic subjects examined biochemically, serum immunoreactive PTH measured in 3 separate immunoassays became supranormal by about age 30 years and appeared to rise further thereafter. Serum alkaline phosphatase activity and creatinine were normal in affected individuals, but serum inorganic phosphate was lower than in unaffected kindred members. Of 5 affected adults older than 40 years who were studied radiographically, 3 had changes suggestive of osteomalacia. In one of 2 hypercalcemic adults who had iliac crest biopsy after tetracycline labeling, a 51-year-old woman, the biopsy confirmed defective skeletal mineralization. The authors concluded that the disorder may not be totally benign, because osteomalacia, perhaps due to mild hypophosphatemia, can develop during adulthood.

paragraphs.text: Hannan et al. (2010) used 24 polymorphic loci in the Oklahoma kindred and found linkage to 10 of 14 informative 19q13 microsatellite loci. The maximum 2-point lod score was 6.92 at theta = 0 for D19S606. Recombinants in 3 affected individuals, together with SNP analysis, narrowed the FBHH3 locus to a 4.1-Mb interval flanked by D19S112 and rs245111, containing 135 protein-coding genes and 24 predicted genes. The syntenic region on mouse chromosome 7 contains 4 Casr-related sequences (Gprc2a-rs1, -rs2, -rs3, and -rs5), but the authors found no human or primate homologs of these genes in the interval. Comparative analysis showed that 2 conserved segments were inverted between mouse and human. It also showed that an 11.6-Mb mouse region containing 35 genes, including the 4 Gprc2a-rs genes, was absent from the human genome, so FBHH3 could not be attributed to Gprc2a-rs abnormalities.

paragraphs.text: Nesbit et al. (2013) performed exome sequencing in an affected individual from each of 2 unrelated FHH3 kindreds, the Oklahoma kindred (FHHOk) and a second kindred (FHHNI). checks.evidence_quote: that all affected Arg15 and consisted of four Arg15Cys, three Arg15His, and four Arg15Leu mutations

checks.claim: In HEK293 cells stably expressing CaSR, the AP2S1 R15C mutant gave an EC50 for extracellular calcium of 2.90 mM, compared with 2.53 mM for wildtype AP2S1.
checks.evidence_quote: Arg15Cys=2.90mM (95% CI 2.85-2.96mM); Arg15His=2.73mM (95% CI 2.66-2.80mM); Arg15Leu=2.86mM (95% CI 2.80-2.93mM); and wild-type AP2σ2 EC50 =2.53mM

checks.claim: In HEK293 cells stably expressing CaSR, the EC50 with the AP2S1 R15C mutant was higher than with vector alone, suggesting a possible dominant-negative effect.
checks.evidence_quote: the EC50 value of cells transfected with the Cys15 AP2S1 mutant were significantly higher than those with vector alone, thereby indicating a possible dominant-negative effect for this AP2S1 mutant

checks.claim: Cells expressing the AP2S1 R15C mutant showed reduced CaSR endocytosis.
checks.evidence_quote: this increased CaSR endocytosis is not observed in cells transfected with the AP2S1 mutant, which instead is associated with decreased CaSR internalisation (Table 3)

paragraphs.text: Howles et al. (2016) reported 3 unrelated probands with symptomatic FHH3, each heterozygous for an AP2S1 mutation resulting in R15C, R15H, or R15L. Cinacalcet corrected the signaling defect caused by the Cys15 mutant in vitro.

checks.claim: Howles et al. (2016) reported 3 unrelated probands with symptomatic FHH3.
checks.evidence_quote: three unrelated probands with familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia who had heterozygous adaptor-related protein complex 2 (AP2), sigma 1 subunit (AP2S1) mutations
checks.explanation: Stated; probands were symptomatic per clinical descriptions.

checks.claim: Each of the 3 FHH3 probands of Howles et al. (2016) was heterozygous for an AP2S1 mutation resulting in R15C, R15H, or R15L.
checks.evidence_quote: Each of the three probands had an AP2S1 mutation causing an Arg15Cys, Arg15His, or Arg15Leu substitution
checks.explanation: Stated; heterozygosity noted in figure legend.

checks.claim: Cinacalcet corrected the signaling defect caused by the AP2S1 Cys15 (R15C) mutant in vitro.
checks.evidence_quote: Cinacalcet (at a concentration of 10 nM) corrected the abnormal intracellular calcium signaling and MAPK responses to extracellular calcium in cells expressing the Cys15, His15, or Leu15 AP2-sigma mutants
